description: The MRC extends far beyond entertainment, shaping multiversal politics, commerce, and culture:
cultural significance: ◦ Events are major cultural touchstones, fostering pride and rivalry among participating species. ◦ Gambling Hubs: Entire planets and space stations are devoted to MRC-backed gambling, shaping local economies.

records.summary: The MRC hosts a variety of high-stakes competitions and races, each uniquely tailored to draw participants and spectators from diverse realities:

description: The MRC hosts a variety of high-stakes competitions and races, each uniquely tailored to draw participants and spectators from diverse realities:
racing formats: ◦ Chaos Circuit: A multiverse-wide grand prix where racers navigate through unstable and dangerous realities, each course dynamically altering mid-race. ◦ Black Run: A high-speed race through the shadowy, chaotic sectors near the Mall, notorious for its hazardous environments and minimal rules. ◦ Species Showdowns: Competitions that pit racers or participants of different species against each other to showcase cultural pride and skill.
interdimensional combat arenas: ◦ Combines vehicular combat with gladiatorial-style battles, where teams and individuals fight for supremacy in ever-changing terrains. ◦ Often includes mechs, custom vehicles, and genetically enhanced creatures as competitors.
seasonal specials: ◦ Royal Chase: An annual event where racers "hunt" a royal-family-sponsored decoy across multiple realities. ◦ Gamblerʼs Gauntlet: A unique blend of chance and skill, where participants must wager resources mid-race for boosts or shortcuts, but miscalculations could lead to elimination.

records.summary: Elves are known for their sophisticated and artistic societies, valuing harmony, beauty, magic, and the pursuit of knowledge. While elven societies vary greatly across different realities, the Elarian Elves of Heimenhearthʼs multiverse are the most influential. As stewards of the Etherflotilla—a cosmic fleet of living ships created after their original planet, Elaria, was mined by dwarves—they travel across realities, maintaining the flora, fauna, and remnants of their homeworld. The Etherflotilla serves as both their sanctuary and a center for multiversal exploration, making them ambassadors, explorers, and diplomats across realms. Elarian Elves maintain complex social structures, with each flotilla vessel often governed by a council of elders, representing noble houses, guilds, and arcane institutions. They are masters of the arcane arts, shaping their environment and using Orilaunʼs magic to create architectural marvels, artwork, and magical artifacts. Each Elarian Elf sees themselves as a protector of their heritage and the magic of Elaria, whether through diplomacy, arcane study, or stewardship of the Etherflotillaʼs natural sanctuaries. ---

records.summary: Humans are among the most adaptable and widespread species across the multiverse, thriving in nearly every environment and society. Their cultures, histories, and philosophies vary immensely, making them one of the most unpredictable species to encounter. Humans exhibit a remarkable ability to learn, innovate, and push boundaries, whether through science, magic, or sheer determination. Their physical forms are diverse, reflecting the many worlds they inhabit, from the technologically advanced cityscapes of Earth to the war-torn frontiers of countless realities. They have an inherent drive to explore and expand, often shaping the destinies of the worlds they call home. Some claim their ingenuity and resilience border on the supernatural, while others believe their presence in nearly every reality is no mere coincidence.

records.summary: “Now we build to heal. Now we shape to honor.” •Timeframe: 1,200 years ago to present •Environment: Sharraʼs deep seas, Memory Reefs, Green Warden cooperation •Philosophy: Restoration, stewardship, identity The modern era of Formcraft is one of integration and recovery. With the safety and spiritual clarity of Sharraʼs Thalassic Ocean, the Kola-Ha refocused their efforts on reverent reconstruction. Forms now prioritize healing, balance, ecology, and inter-species diplomacy. Many are designed for customization, emotional bonding, or cross-species tutoring. These Forms are often lighter, subtler, and more symbolic—though still powerful.

records.summary: - Historical Storage: Employing a specialized coral species that encodes and stores memories and information within its skeletal structure, acting as a living library that records the history, knowledge, and experiences of the Kola-Ha. - Generational Transmission: Young Kola-Ha interact with these memory reefs to absorb the knowledge and wisdom of previous generations through a mystical, experiential connection. Through this fascinating confluence of biology and magic, the Kola-Ha have illuminated an alternative path toward progress, one where technology and ecology swim side by side in a mesmerizing dance of light and life, revealing the unbounded potentials lurking within the depths of imagination and the sea alike.

records.summary: (The Warrior Castes – Built for battle, these Moravi are relentless frontline fighters.)

description: (The Warrior Castes – Built for battle, these Moravi are relentless frontline fighters.)
appearance: ◦ Their thickened exoskeletons appear dark brown, deep crimson, or obsidian black, often featuring natural spiked ridges or reinforced plating. ◦ Their mandibles are larger and stronger, suited for crushing armor and bone.
traits: ◦ Hardened Carapace: Gain +1 AC and resistance to non-magical slashing damage. ◦ Battle Frenzy: Once per short rest, when reduced to half HP or lower, gain advantage on attack rolls for one round. ◦ Colonyʼs Might: When adjacent to an ally, add +1 to melee damage rolls. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Dreadcarapace Moravi serve as the primary defenders and warriors of their colonies. ◦ Many become mercenaries, bodyguards, or commanders in multiversal conflicts.

records.summary: (The Silent Striders – Built for stealth, speed, and infiltration.)

description: (The Silent Striders – Built for stealth, speed, and infiltration.)
appearance: ◦ Lighter exoskeletons in ashen gray, sandy brown, or pale white, allowing them to blend into shadows and dim environments. ◦ Slender, elongated limbs optimized for quick, silent movement.
traits: ◦ Shadow Walker: Gain advantage on Stealth checks when in low-light environments. ◦ Wall Crawler: Gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. ◦ Ambush Instinct: Once per combat, when attacking from stealth, add +1d6 damage. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Hollowborn Moravi are often used as scouts, infiltrators, and messengers. ◦ Their hives specialize in espionage, silent warfare, and securing resources.

records.summary: The Moravi have evolved into distinct subspecies, each specializing in different survival tactics, warfare styles, or labor divisions. These variations have developed based on environmental adaptations, hive structures, and the specific needs of their colonies. Each subspecies has unique physical traits, abilities, and cultural distinctions, making them well-suited for different roles in the multiversal ecosystem.

Known for low-cost housing, clan festivals, rewilding rituals, and accessible proximity to Neon culture. •Clans: Heavy presence of Veridokka, The Union, and Urban Adrenaline. Laurasgate (Out-By) •Tone: Tranquil, boundary-crossing outpost blending controlled wilderness with light urban infrastructure. •Significance: Seat of the Out-By Council, the mediating force between Wildclade and Urbanclade ideologies. •Culture: Meditative, political, ritual-rich. Clans often leave emissaries here. •Clans: Dominated by Veridokka, The Union, and diplomat arms of larger clans.

records.summary: Orc society developed out of rebellion and survival, shaped by their history as a genetically engineered species and their journey to freedom. The largest slave uprising against the Goblin empire was led by the orcs, and since that victory, they have become one of the most widespread species in the multiverse, found in countless worlds and adapting to myriad cultures and environments. Orcs value strength, resilience, and independence, organizing themselves into tribes or clans that are often led by the most capable and battle-tested chieftain. Each tribe has its own unique traditions, influenced by the environment it occupies. Orc settlements are fortified and built with defense in mind, and orcs are highly skilled in hunting, craftsmanship, and combat. They work with materials readily available to them, often favoring bone, hide, and metals shaped through brute strength. ---

records.summary: •Rakuuta are a cousin species of kobolds, possessing reptilian features and standing between 3 and 4.5 feet tall. •They exhibit nimble, dexterous hands and possess strong, lithe bodies that grant them remarkable agility and precision in movement. •Their appearance is marked by scales covering their bodies, predominantly in shades of gray and green, with distinct patterns reminiscent of their reptilian heritage. •Rakuuta feature characteristic facial markings resembling a dark bird around their eyes, enhancing their keen vision in low-light conditions and a hardened 'beak'. •Their physical attributes make them excellent climbers, a trait utilized when navigating both urban and wild landscapes.

records.summary: Ratmen society revolves around survival, community, and opportunism. While many live in sprawling underground tunnel networks, hidden enclaves, or abandoned ruins, others integrate into cities as scavengers, traders, or thieves. Their settlements are often labyrinthine, with interconnected burrows and pathways designed to be defensible and easily escapable in times of danger. Unlike some species with rigid hierarchies, Ratmen operate in loose, adaptable clans, with leadership shifting based on circumstance rather than bloodline. Those who prove the most cunning, resourceful, or persuasive often find themselves leading for a time, though any leader who grows too complacent is quickly replaced. Their society thrives on barter, knowledge-sharing, and the rapid exchange of goods and services. Despite their sometimes chaotic or secretive nature, Ratmen are highly cooperative within their own groups, often using a shared network of hidden tunnels and contacts across worlds to communicate and trade. records.summary: (The Infiltrators – Silent assassins and information brokers, excelling in deception.)

description: (The Infiltrators – Silent assassins and information brokers, excelling in deception.)
appearance: ◦ Matte black or dark gray exoskeletons, absorbing light to make them nearly invisible in darkness. ◦ Smoother, streamlined body structure designed for stealth and rapid movement. ◦ Dull, almost featureless eyes that make their expressions hard to read.
traits: ◦ Shadowstep: Once per short rest, you can move 10 feet as a reaction when an enemy is unaware of your presence. ◦ Silent Presence: Gain advantage on Stealth checks and cannot be detected by scent.

records.summary: The Rohai reject rigid societal structures, instead embracing fluid, ever-changing communities that shift based on opportunity, necessity, and survival. Their settlements are often nomadic, adaptable, or hidden, existing in the shadows of larger civilizations, on the fringes of lawless spaceports, or within forgotten ruins. Rather than forming traditional governments, Rohai leadership is based on merit, cunning, and adaptability. Those who can outthink and outmaneuver others naturally rise to prominence, only to be replaced when someone sharper comes along. Despite their chaotic tendencies, Rohai value companionship and teamwork, forming tight-knit survival groups called "Clutches." These Clutches function as temporary families, bound by trust, mutual benefit, and shared survival goals. While most species seek wealth, power, or conquest, Rohai seek survival, freedom, and the next big opportunity.

records.summary: (Swamp Stalkers – Adapted to toxic wetlands, jungles, and sewer-like ecosystems.)

description: (Swamp Stalkers – Adapted to toxic wetlands, jungles, and sewer-like ecosystems.)
appearance: ◦ Mottled green, brown, or yellow exoskeletons, blending with wetland environments. ◦ Slick, water-resistant chitin, allowing them to move through mud and water effortlessly. ◦ More prominent antennae, used to sense vibrations and chemical changes in the air.
traits: ◦ Swamp Camouflage: Gain advantage on Stealth checks in natural environments. ◦ Amphibious Adaptation: Can hold breath for up to 30 minutes and swim at full movement speed. ◦ Viral Resistance: Gain advantage on saving throws against diseases and parasites. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Muckdweller Rohai are ambushers, survivalists, and alchemists, mastering the toxic and unpredictable nature of swamps and wetlands. ◦ Many become guides, assassins, or toxin-harvesters, using their innate resistance to survive hostile environments.

records.summary: (Industrial Survivors – Adapted to scrapyards, polluted ruins, and toxic wastelands.)

description: (Industrial Survivors – Adapted to scrapyards, polluted ruins, and toxic wastelands.)
appearance: ◦ Rough, rust-colored exoskeletons that have hardened over time, providing additional resistance to environmental hazards. ◦ Patches of corroded plating, reinforced by natural secretions that resist rust and decay. ◦ Dark, reflective eyes adapted for navigating smog-filled environments.
traits: ◦ Toxic Resilience: Gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against inhaled toxins. ◦ Scrap Instincts: When scavenging, you can identify valuable or functional components instantly. ◦ Wasteland Tenacity: Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP, you may drop to 1 HP instead if the attack was not critical. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Rustborn Rohai thrive in industrial ruins, mechanical scrapyards, and post-apocalyptic wastelands. ◦ Many become tinkerers, mechanics, or scavengers, using their natural resilience to profit from abandoned technology.
